en: I transferred the rent to the landlord this morning.
tamil: இன்னைக்கு காலையில வீட்டு உரிமையாளருக்கு வாடகை அனுப்பிட்டேன்.
context: Telling your flatmate the rent is done.
explain: 'This morning' with past tense is used when the morning is over.
usage: Use it with a flatmate or family member to confirm rent payment.
leelaQ: Do you rent a house or live in your own house?
answer: I live in my own house.

en: Is the interest rate fixed or floating?
tamil: வட்டி விகிதம் நிலையானதா, மாறக்கூடியதா?
context: Asking a loan officer.
explain: 'Fixed' means it does not change. 'Floating' means it can change.
usage: Ask it before you sign any loan paper.
leelaQ: Why do some people like a fixed rate?
answer: They like it because the payment stays the same.

en: May I see your ID proof, please?
tamil: உங்க அடையாள அட்டையை பார்க்கலாமா?
context: A bank staff member asking a customer.
explain: 'May I ...?' is a formal, polite request used in offices.
usage: Bank and office staff say this before they process a request.
leelaQ: What ID proofs do you carry with you?
answer: I carry my Aadhaar card and driving licence.

en: Many people in my village use UPI for small payments.
tamil: எங்க ஊர்ல நிறைய பேர் சின்ன பேமெண்டுக்கு UPI பயன்படுத்தறாங்க.
context: Telling a friend about digital payment use.
explain: 'Many people' takes a plural verb: use, not uses.
usage: Use it when you talk about how people pay in your area.
leelaQ: How has UPI changed life in small towns?
answer: Now even tea shops take payments on the phone.

en: If I save every month, I will buy a laptop soon.
tamil: ஒவ்வொரு மாசமும் சேமிச்சா சீக்கிரம் லேப்டாப் வாங்கிடுவேன்.
context: Telling a friend about a goal.
explain: 'If' + present, then 'will' shows a real possibility.
usage: Use it when you talk about a goal you are saving for.
leelaQ: What are you saving money for?
answer: I am saving money for a laptop.

en: I don't use credit cards because I spend too much.
tamil: நான் அதிகமா செலவு பண்ணுவேன்னு கிரெடிட் கார்டு பயன்படுத்தறதில்ல.
context: Explaining your money habit.
explain: 'Because' gives the reason. 'Don't use' is the negative present.
usage: Use it when someone asks why you do not have a credit card.
leelaQ: Do you spend more when you shop online?
answer: Yes, I sometimes buy things I do not need.

en: How much did you pay for this?
tamil: இதுக்கு நீங்க எவ்வளவு கொடுத்தீங்க?
context: Asking a friend about a new thing.
explain: 'How much did you pay' asks the price of something bought.
usage: Ask it with friends when you admire something new they bought.
leelaQ: What was the last thing you bought and how much was it?
answer: I bought a bag and it cost five hundred rupees.

en: The bank is giving a good rate on fixed deposits.
tamil: வங்கி ஃபிக்ஸட் டெபாசிட்டுக்கு நல்ல வட்டி தருது.
context: Telling your uncle about an offer.
explain: Present continuous shows an offer that is available now.
usage: Use it with family when you share news about a savings offer.
leelaQ: What do older people in your family do with their savings?
answer: They keep it in fixed deposits.

en: Wait here while I withdraw some cash.
tamil: நான் கொஞ்சம் பணம் எடுக்கற வரை இங்க இருங்க.
context: Asking a friend to wait outside an ATM.
explain: 'While' connects two actions at the same time.
usage: Say it to a friend or driver when you go to an ATM.
leelaQ: Do you feel safe using an ATM at night?
answer: No, I prefer to go in the daytime.

en: My account got blocked after three wrong PIN attempts.
tamil: மூணு தடவை தப்பான பின் போட்டதுனால என் கணக்கு பிளாக் ஆயிடுச்சு.
context: Reporting a problem at the bank.
explain: 'Got blocked' is a common spoken passive form.
usage: Use it at the bank or on a helpline when a card or account stops working.
leelaQ: What would you do if your account is blocked?
answer: I would go to the bank with my ID.

en: We have cleared all our credit card dues.
tamil: எங்க கிரெடிட் கார்டு பாக்கி எல்லாம் அடைச்சிட்டோம்.
context: Sharing good news with a friend.
explain: 'Have cleared' shows the work is complete now.
usage: Use it when you tell friends or family you are free of debt.
leelaQ: How does it feel when you finish paying a loan?
answer: It feels like a big weight is gone.

en: Can I pay the school fee in instalments?
tamil: பள்ளிக் கட்டணத்தை தவணையில கட்டலாமா?
context: Asking the school office.
explain: 'In instalments' means in smaller parts over time.
usage: Ask it at a school or college office when the full fee is hard to pay.
leelaQ: Why do people like paying in instalments?
answer: Because it is easier to pay small amounts.

en: A good budget helps you avoid debt.
tamil: நல்ல பட்ஜெட் கடன் வராம தவிர்க்க உதவும்.
context: Giving a friend money advice.
explain: 'Helps you avoid' is a useful pattern: help + person + verb.
usage: Use it when you give simple money advice to younger people.
leelaQ: What is one tip you can give a new college student about money?
answer: Write down every expense and spend carefully.

en: You can check your balance on the mobile app.
tamil: மொபைல் ஆப்ல உங்க இருப்பை பார்க்கலாம்.
context: Helping an elderly person with banking.
explain: 'Can' shows that something is possible.
usage: Use it when you teach an elder a simple banking step.
leelaQ: Have you taught anyone to use a banking app?
answer: Yes, I taught my mother to use it.

en: Gold is not cheap anymore.
tamil: தங்கம் இப்போ மலிவு இல்ல.
context: Talking about jewellery prices.
explain: 'Not ... anymore' shows something was true before but is not true now.
usage: Use it when you talk about prices with family before a purchase.
leelaQ: What was cheap in the past but is costly now?
answer: Tea and bus tickets were cheap in the past.

en: Why is the electricity bill so high this month?
tamil: இந்த மாசம் கரண்ட் பில் ஏன் இவ்வளவு அதிகம்?
context: Asking your family at home.
explain: 'So high' stresses that the amount is surprising.
usage: Use it at home, or with the electricity office, when a bill looks wrong.
leelaQ: How can a family reduce its electricity use?
answer: We can switch off fans and lights when we leave a room.

en: He paid the vegetable seller by scanning a QR code.
tamil: அவர் QR கோடை ஸ்கேன் பண்ணி காய்கறிக்காரருக்கு பணம் கொடுத்தார்.
context: Describing how people pay in a market.
explain: 'By scanning' shows the way something was done.
usage: Use it when you tell a story about digital payments in daily life.
leelaQ: Do vegetable sellers near you accept phone payments?
answer: Yes, many of them have a QR code board.

en: Could you lower the interest a little?
tamil: வட்டியை கொஞ்சம் குறைக்க முடியுமா?
context: Negotiating with a loan agent.
explain: 'A little' makes the request softer and more polite.
usage: Use it politely when you talk to a loan agent or a lender.
leelaQ: Do you think it is okay to negotiate with a bank?
answer: Yes, it is okay to ask for a better rate.

en: I'll check my bank statement tonight.
tamil: இன்னைக்கு ராத்திரி என் வங்கி அறிக்கையை பார்ப்பேன்.
context: Promising to look into a payment.
explain: 'I'll' is the short form of 'I will'. It is common in speech.
usage: Say it when someone asks about a payment you need to verify.
leelaQ: How often do you go through your bank statement?
answer: I go through it once a month.

en: My mother keeps a small savings box at home.
tamil: என் அம்மா வீட்டுல ஒரு சின்ன உண்டியல் வச்சிருக்காங்க.
context: Telling a friend about a family habit.
explain: Simple present with 'keeps' shows a regular habit.
usage: Use it when you talk about saving habits in your family.
leelaQ: Did you save coins in a box when you were a child?
answer: Yes, I saved coins in a small box.

en: I can't afford a new phone right now.
tamil: இப்போ புது போன் வாங்க என்னால முடியாது.
context: Explaining to a friend why you will not buy.
explain: 'Can't afford' means you do not have enough money for something.
usage: Use it honestly with friends or sellers when something is beyond your budget.
leelaQ: What would you like to buy if money was not a problem?
answer: I would buy a new phone and a laptop.

en: Is the bank open on the second Saturday of the month?
tamil: மாசத்தோட இரண்டாவது சனிக்கிழமை வங்கி திறந்திருக்குமா?
context: Asking a bank clerk about weekend working days.
explain: Many banks in India are closed on the second Saturday, so people check first.
usage: Ask it at the bank gate or on a helpline to plan your visit.
leelaQ: When do you find time to visit the bank?
answer: I go on Saturday mornings.

en: I have set a monthly limit for my spending.
tamil: என் செலவுக்கு ஒரு மாசாந்திர வரம்பு வச்சிருக்கேன்.
context: Telling a friend about your money control.
explain: 'Have set' shows a rule you made that still applies.
usage: Use it when you discuss money habits with friends.
leelaQ: How do you control your spending?
answer: I set a limit and track it in a notebook.

en: Prices are rising, so we are cutting small expenses.
tamil: விலை ஏறிட்டே போகுது, அதனால சின்ன செலவுகளை குறைக்கிறோம்.
context: Explaining a family decision.
explain: 'So' connects a cause and its result.
usage: Use it when you explain why a family is spending less.
leelaQ: Which small expenses can you cut easily?
answer: I can cut eating outside and online orders.

en: I paid the full amount and got a discount.
tamil: நான் முழு தொகையை கட்டினேன், தள்ளுபடி கிடைச்சுது.
context: Telling a friend about a good deal.
explain: Two past actions joined by 'and'.
usage: Use it when you share a money-saving experience.
leelaQ: Have you ever got a discount for paying early?
answer: Yes, I got a small discount on my insurance.
